why.title: Why CostTrek
why.lead: Moving city or country is one of the biggest money decisions you will make — and most cost-of-living figures online are guesses. CostTrek turns them into an honest, like-for-like comparison of rent, taxes, salaries and everyday life, so you can see what a move really means before you commit.
why.p1d: US costs anchored to BEA and Census, economies from the World Bank — not scraped guesses.
why.p2d: See the income you would need elsewhere to keep the same standard of living.
why.p3d: Taxes, visas, safety, climate and quality of life across every city, in five languages.

home.popularSub: The relocation routes people search for most.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.cityCostQ: How much does it cost to live in {city}?
faq.cityCostA: {city}'s cost-of-living index is {index} (US average = 100) — about {pct}% {word} than a typical US city. A one-bedroom apartment in the centre costs around ${rent} per month.
faq.cityLivingQ: What are the average living costs in {city}?
faq.cityLivingA: Living costs in {city} are about {pct}% {word} than the US average — its cost-of-living index is {index} (US = 100). Monthly living expenses scale with that, and housing is the biggest line: a one-bedroom in the centre runs around ${rent}. See the category breakdown above for where the money goes.
faq.cityRentQ: What is the average rent in {city}?
faq.cityRentA: A one-bedroom in the city centre averages about ${rentCentre} per month, and around ${rentOutside} outside the centre.
faq.cityTaxQ: What taxes would I pay in {country}?
faq.cityTaxA: {country} has a top income-tax rate of {incomeTax}% and a VAT or sales tax of {vat}%. See the taxes section above for the full breakdown.
faq.cityClimateQ: What is the weather like in {city}?
faq.cityClimateA: {city} averages around {jan} in January and {jul} in July, with roughly {sunny} sunny days a year.
faq.citySafetyA: {city} scores {safety} out of 100 on our safety index, where higher means safer.
faq.cmpMoveQ: Moving from {a} to {b}: cheaper or more expensive?
faq.cmpMoveA: Moving from {a} to {b}, your cost of living will be roughly {pct}% {word}. {b}’s cost-of-living index is {ib} versus {ia} for {a} (US = 100). Use the salary tool above to see the income you’d need to keep the same lifestyle.
faq.cmpCheaperA: {b} is about {pct}% {word} than {a} overall — its cost-of-living index is {ib} versus {ia} for {a}.
faq.cmpSalaryQ: How much do you need to earn in {b} to live like in {a}?
faq.cmpSalaryA: To keep the same standard of living, a ${salary} salary in {a} is worth about ${equivalent} in {b}. Enter your own figure in the calculator above.
faq.cmpTaxADiff: {lowCountry} has the lower top income-tax rate — {lowRate}% versus {highRate}% in {highCountry}.
faq.cmpTaxASame: Both cities are in the same country, so national income tax ({rate}%) and VAT are identical; only local cost of living differs.
